Bull spike out of the base: bar 84 (open 1916.51, high 2293.8, close 2252.16) clears the base by a wide margin, bar 85 closes 2326.32, bar 86 spikes to 2771 and closes 2515.3. No exact horizontal boundary is claimed for this impulsive leg.

Post-spike consolidation and channel-like portion of the bull leg: bars 87-111 overlap between low 2357.18 (bar 99) and high 2680 (bar 107) while keeping higher lows, so the leg is channel-like rather than a clean spike.

Two-bar bear reversal attempt at the bull high: bar 117 makes a new high 2850 and closes 2775.61, then bars 118-119 turn down and bar 119 closes 2684.16 near its low. Higher high over the 2771 spike high (bar 86) plus only two bear bars means this is a potential reversal pattern, not a confirmed reversal.

evidence_for: Higher swing lows dominate after bar 84: 2111 (bar 85 low), 2325.31 (bar 86 low), 2357.18 (bar 99 low), 2358.62 (bar 111 low), 2435.72 (bar 107 low).
Higher swing highs over the same span: 2348.02 (bar 85), 2771 (bar 86), 2680 (bar 107), 2850 (bar 117).
Bull bodies carry the advance: bar 84 opens 1916.51 and closes 2252.16, bar 107 opens 2437 and prints 2680, and bars 113-117 run from 2446.22 to a 2775.61 close.
The current two-bar set-back (bars 118-119) is no deeper than the repeated pullbacks inside the 87-111 band, which is normal pullback behavior inside a bull leg.
evidence_against: The leg since bar 84 spends about 25 bars (87-111) inside a two-sided 2357.18-2680 band, so the leg is at least as range-like as trend-like and could be classified trading-range/channel rather than bull-trend.
Momentum faded at the highs: bar 86 spiked to 2771 but closed 2515.3 with a long upper tail, and the 2643-2850 top area shows overlapping bars rather than clean trend bars.
Bar 119 closes near its low (2684.16 in a 2641.37-2786.81 range) after a marginal new high 2850 versus the 2771 spike high, so an MTR from the high is not excluded.
The first 84 bars of the window are bearish then rangebound, so the bull case rests only on roughly the last 36 bars.
transition_conditions: Bull continuation is supported if a bar closes above 2786.81 (bar 119 high) and then above 2850 (bar 117 high) with a strong bull body and little overlap.
A close below 2641.37 (bar 119 low), then below 2435.72 (bar 107 low) and 2358.62 (bar 111 low), would break the sequence of higher lows and weaken the bull read.
A close below 2325.31 (bar 86 low) would negate the post-base breakout structure and favor a major-trend-reversal or trading-range classification.
If subsequent bars keep overlapping and closing mid-range around 2600-2800 for many sessions, the read shifts from bull-trend/channel toward trading-range/range.

observations: Window covers 120 closed D1 bars from open 1779926400000 to the final close 1790294399999; window low is 1368.42 (bar 10, close 1780790399999) and window high is 2850 (bar 117, close 1789948800000), a 108% advance from low to high.

structures.description: Bear breakout of the bars 1-5 range 1958.77-2042.37, with five consecutive bear closes down to the 1368.42 low; bar 6 opens 2006.06 and closes 1859.02, bar 10 closes 1568.55.
Sell-climax reversal bar at the 1368.42 low: close 1568.55 with a 200.13-point lower tail, ending the bear spike and starting the basing process.
Post-spike two-sided range with heavy overlap and alternating closes; high 1845.09 (bar 19), higher low 1512.91 (bar 30), roughly 1500-1850 area.
Bull leg from the 1597.72 low (bar 36) to the 1944.39 high (bar 49), continued by a pullback low of 1803.74 (bar 51).
34-bar overlapping range between 1803.74 (bar 51 low) and 1974.46 (bar 61 high); the bar 61 probe above 1974.46 failed and closed 1891.41, and bars 73 and 80 are very small doji bars.
Bull spike out of the 1800-1975 range: bar 84 rises from 1916.51 to close 2252.16, and bar 86 spikes to 2771 before closing 2515.30 (buy climax with a 255.70-point upper tail).
27-bar range after the spike between 2357.18 (bar 98 low) and 2557.46 (bar 92 high); bar 107 overshoots to 2680 but closes 2514.72 back inside the range.
Four-bar breakout above the 2557.46 range top: closes 2612.02, 2632.98, 2642.90 and 2775.61, with bar 117 printing the window high 2850 (74.39-point upper tail).

Three-bar pullback from bar 118 high 2776.18 to bar 120 low 2633.31 that holds above the 2557.46 breakout level; bar 119's low 2641.37 undercuts bar 117's low 2641.70 and bar 120 closes 2686.59 near the top of its range.

evidence_for: Acceptance above a multi-week range: four consecutive closes (2612.02, 2632.98, 2642.90, 2775.61) above the 2557.46 top of the 27-bar bars 87-113 range, with a new window high at 2850 (bar 117).
Swing progression is upward across the window: higher lows 1368.42 -> 1512.91 -> 1803.74 -> 2357.18 paired with higher highs 1944.39 -> 1974.46 -> 2771 -> 2850.

The pullback after the breakout is being bought above the breakout level: bars 118-120 hold low 2633.31, and bar 120 closes 2686.59, 129 points above 2557.46 and in the upper 81% of its own 66.08 range.

The 27-bar range (bars 87-113) resolved upward with follow-through bars 115 and 116 (closes 2632.98 and 2642.90) rather than immediately reversing, unlike the failed bar 61 (1974.46) and bar 107 (2680) probes inside earlier ranges.
evidence_against: The strongest counterargument is that the trend keeps producing spiking highs that are not held: bar 86 reached 2771 with a 255.70-point upper tail and was followed by 27 sideways bars, and bar 117 now shows the same shape with high 2850 and close 2775.61 (74.39-point tail), so the current 'breakout' may be another overshoot rather than a durable spike.

Trading-range behaviour dominates the window: bars 11-35, 50-83 and 87-113 are three multi-week ranges covering roughly 86 of 120 bars, so this market has repeatedly reverted to range after every strong leg, which weakens a trend-continuation label.

The pullback is large relative to the leg: 216.69 points (~7.6%) from 2850 to 2633.31 in only three bars, and bar 119's low 2641.37 undercuts the low 2641.70 of the breakout bar 117, a sign that the spike's momentum is already being absorbed.

The last 20 bars are only net +207 (bar 101 close 2479.28 to bar 120 close 2686.59) while containing both a new high 2850 and a deep dip to 2358.62 (bar 111), i.e., two-sided rather than one-directional pressure.
transition_conditions: Two or more consecutive closes above 2776.18 (bar 118 high) would confirm the bars 114-117 leg as a continuing spike and keep the read as bull breakout.
A daily close back below 2557.46 (the bars 87-113 range top) would mark the breakout as failed and revert the primary read to trading-range with an upper boundary near 2850.
A close below bar 120's low 2633.31 followed by a lower high below 2776.18 would shift the always-in to short and raise the higher-high MTR-like interpretation of 2771 versus 2850.
Continued overlapping closes between roughly 2633 and 2776 with small bodies would move the phase from breakout-spike toward channel or range without changing the bullish regime label.
